rationale: Strengthen the first question's account by replacing a supplied fixture with the public client contract. The new harness wraps the leader, lets the application report applied progress through Advance while it is still applying the committed configuration change, campaigns and issues ReadIndex through the Node interface, and only then calls ApplyConfChange; the verified draft run shows the postponement (pending_reads 1, no ReadState) and then, after the applied change performs the leader's first term-2 commit (committed 10 -> 11, committed_entry_term 2), still no ReadState for the request and pending_reads 1 - the witness through the documented API rather than internal fields. One execution is requested.

experiment.revision_reason: The harness now drives the scenario through the public Node/Ready contract instead of a supplied applied index: the application consumes the wrapped leader's Readys and calls Advance while it is still applying the committed configuration change (node.go:166-187 permits this), campaigns, issues its ReadIndex request, and only then calls ApplyConfChange for that change. The comparisons read the delivered ReadStates and the leader's own status rather than internal fields.

scope.description: Observe a postponed ReadIndex request through the Node interface of a wrapped leader whose application has reported applied progress past a committed configuration change without having applied it yet, and then applies that change: the decisive observation is whether any Ready delivers the ReadState for the request once the leader has committed an entry of its term.
assumptions: The wrapped node 1 is a four-voter group {1,2,3,4} whose storage holds ten term-1 entries with the last one removing voter 4, and a persisted HardState committing index 10.

Voter 2 is a bare raft instance whose acknowledgements are delivered; voter 3 is a bare raft instance whose append acknowledgements are held (delayed), and voter 4 is unreachable, so the leader cannot commit under the configuration it still has.

The application consumes Readys, writes entries, hard state and snapshots to the leader's storage, calls Advance (reported applied progress through index 10) and only later calls ApplyConfChange for the change it observed; the campaign and the ReadIndex request are issued through the Node interface.

experiment.prefix: Build the wrapped leader over the four-voter fixture, pump its Readys (persisting buffers and calling Advance) without calling ApplyConfChange so that applied index 10 is reported while the tracker still holds voters=(1 2 3 4); campaign through the Node interface and pump until it reports StateLeader at term 2 with its term entry acknowledged only by voter 2; issue ReadIndex with context A and pump; then call ApplyConfChange for the committed removal of voter 4 and pump, recording every ReadState the Readys deliver.
experiment.requirement: A ReadIndex request that a leader accepts by postponing must be answered once the leader has committed an entry of its term, whichever path performs that commit (raft.go:1550-1554 for the MsgAppResp path, raft.go:2013-2028 for the switchToConfig path), because the helper that discharges the duty is guarded only by committedEntryInCurrentTerm() (raft.go:2127-2145).
experiment.responsibility: raft (target): the leader accepted the request and is the producer of the answer; the application followed the documented Ready/Advance/ApplyConfChange sequence.

comparisons.description: Premise: the wrapped node became leader at term 2 through the Node campaign path.
Premise: the ReadIndex request issued through the Node interface was postponed (no entry of the leader's term committed yet).
Witness: applying the committed change performed the leader's first commit of term 2 (committed 10 -> 11 with committed_entry_term 2), yet no Ready delivered a ReadState for context A.
Witness: the postponed request is still held after that commit.
